name: Barnyard grass
local: Antena, bayakibok, biyuro, humay humay, marapagay, naik, palay pato, telebisyon
stop: Sow clean seed, flood the field early and keep the water steady, and pull the plants that slip past before their heads open; it drops seed within about two months.

name: Weedy rice
stop: Sow certified seed, never seed kept from a field that had it. Prepare the land twice so its seed sprouts and dies, transplant where it is bad, and pull plants that grow taller, flower early or carry red, awned grains before they shatter.

name: Chinese sprangletop
local: Kuring kuring, marapagay, maroy paroy, salay maya, palay maya
stop: It sprouts on moist soil but not under water, so keep water on the field from early on, and pull or spray it while young; older plants shrug off many grass killers.

name: Echinochloa glabrescens
local: Telebisyon, antena, dawa dawa, marapagay, paray paray, humay humay
stop: Use clean seed and early, steady flooding, and hand pull plants that look like rice but have no ligule before they seed.

name: Jungle rice
stop: It sprouts on moist, not flooded, soil: flood rice early, mulch or hoe upland crops, and do not let it seed on bunds and field edges.

name: Wrinkle grass
local: Ipot doron, bika bika, bulo bulo, gulong lapas, limba limba, salsaladay, tinitrigo, trigo trigohan
stop: Keep standing water on the paddy early and level the field so no dry spots are left; pull it before the dark seed heads ripen.

name: Purple nutsedge
stop: Its tubers live for years in the soil: plow and harrow several times in the dry season so new shoots keep using up the tubers, then shade it with a crop that closes fast, mulch or plastic.

name: Smallflower umbrella sedge
local: Baong baong, bulo butones, payong payong, siraw siraw, treskantos, tuhog dalang, ubod ubod
stop: It sprouts on saturated soil before the field floods: flood early and deep enough to cover the soil, and pull it before the round heads ripen; one plant makes thousands of tiny seeds.

name: Rice flatsedge
local: Payong payong, siraw siraw, taga taga
stop: Flood rice early and hoe it young in upland fields; it ripens seed fast, so pull it before the heads turn brown.

name: Globe fringerush
local: Bungot bungot, buntot pusa, gumi, siraw siraw, sirisibayas, sumpana balik
stop: Keep water on the field early and level it well; pull the tufts before the round brown heads drop their seed.

name: Heartshape false pickerelweed
stop: Its seeds sprout under water, so flooding alone does not stop it: pull it early, before it flowers, and level the field so a pre emergence herbicide covers it evenly.

name: Gooseweed
local: Balabalanob, burat aso, mais mais, silisilihan
stop: Keep the water on early and pull it young; it ripens seed in the paddy within weeks.

name: Seedbox
stop: Flood the field early, pull it young, and spare the small black Altica beetle, which eats its leaves.

name: False daisy
stop: It sprouts on moist, open soil: flood rice early, mulch upland crops and pull it before it seeds.

name: Water hyacinth
stop: Rake it out of canals and ponds before it reaches the paddy, put a screen at the water inlet, and compost what you pull away from the water.

name: Bermuda grass
local: Bakbaka, buku buku, galud galud, kawad kawad
stop: It grows back from runners and buried stems: plow and dry the runners in the sun, plow once more before planting, and never carry soil with its runners into a clean field.

name: Carabao grass
local: Kauat kauat, lakatan, maligoy, pad pad, kolokawayan, bantotan, kulape, laau laau
stop: It runs along the ground and roots at each joint: slash it often, grow a cover crop, and let the crop or the trees shade it out.

name: Crowfoot grass
local: Damong balang, bayakibok, krus krusan, sabong sabongan, tugot manok
stop: Hoe or pull it while young, mulch the rows, and mow field edges before it seeds.

name: Goosegrass
local: Bakis bakisan, bang angan, bikad bikad, bila bila, palagtiki, parangis, paragis, sabung sabungan, sambali
stop: Its tough roots hold on: pull or hoe it young, mulch the rows, and switch herbicide groups, since it learns to survive one group fast.

name: Knotgrass
local: Bakbaka, barit, damong ube, lubid lubid, malit kalabaw, ragitnit
stop: It creeps by runners in wet ground: plow and leave the runners to dry in the sun at land preparation, keep bunds and canals clean, and hold deep water early.

name: Kodo millet
stop: Flood early and keep the field level; pull plants on bunds and dry spots before they seed.

name: Southern crabgrass
stop: A stale seedbed before planting kills its first flush; mulch or hoe the rows while it is small, and do not let it seed along the edges.

name: Southern cutgrass
stop: It spreads by creeping stems in wet ground: rake out the runners and let them dry at land preparation, and keep canals and bunds free of it.

name: Torpedo grass
local: Tagik tagik, buwag buwag, murag bermuda, maralaya, luy a luy a, sabilau, luya luyahan
stop: Its underground runners break and grow again: plow when the soil is dry, leave the runners to dry in the sun, repeat before planting, and keep it off the bunds.

name: Cyperus compactus
stop: Keep the paddy flooded early and pull it while young; dig out older clumps with their base so they do not regrow.

name: Annual sedge
stop: Hoe or pull it while young and keep the field edges clean; it seeds quickly in moist, open ground.

name: Finger flatsedge
stop: Keep the paddy flooded early and pull it while young; dig out older clumps with their base so they do not regrow.

name: Slender cyperus
stop: Keep the paddy flooded early and pull it while young; dig out older clumps with their base so they do not regrow.

name: Haspan flatsedge
local: Balabalangutan, barsanga, bungot bungot, manik manikan
stop: Keep the paddy flooded early and pull it young, before the loose heads seed; dig out older clumps with their base.

name: Shingle flatsedge
stop: Keep the paddy flooded early and pull it while young; dig out older clumps with their base so they do not regrow.

name: Forked fimbry
stop: Flood early and level the field; pull plants on bunds and high spots before they seed.

name: Giant bulrush
stop: It spreads by thick underground runners in wet, low spots: dig out the clumps with their runners at land preparation, and level or drain the low spots.

name: Rock bulrush
stop: Hold water on the paddy early and pull it young; dig out old clumps with their base.

name: Alyce clover
stop: Hoe or pull it young on bunds and dry spots, before its jointed pods ripen.

name: Blistering ammannia
stop: Keep standing water early and pull it before the many small seed capsules along its stem ripen.

name: Asian spiderflower
local: Apoy apoyan, balabalanoyan, hulaya, kabau, lampotaki, tantandok, sili silihan
stop: Hoe or pull it young and mulch the rows; do not let its long pods ripen.

name: Balloon vine
local: Alalayon, bangkolon, lubo lobohan, parol parolan, paltu paltukan, parya aso, paspalya
stop: Pull the vines before the papery balloons ripen, and keep the field edges clean where it climbs.

name: Basilicum polystachyon
stop: Pull it from bunds and moist edges before it seeds, and hoe it in upland fields.

name: Benghal dayflower
stop: Pull it out whole and carry it off the field, since stem pieces root again; it even sets seed from flowers under the soil, so mulch and a crop that closes fast help most.

name: Chamber bitter
local: Apoy apoyan, ibaiba an, lurulaioan, minuhminuh, payog, sursampalok, tabi, takum takum, talindanon, turutalikod
stop: Hoe it young and mulch the rows; it ripens seed within weeks under its branches.

name: Climbing dayflower
stop: Pull whole plants and carry them off the field, since stem pieces left on moist soil root again.

name: East Indian jute
stop: Pull or hoe it while young on bunds and upland fields, before its pods split.

name: Creeping water primrose
stop: Pull the floating stems out of canals and the paddy before transplanting; pieces root again, so carry them out of the field.

name: Cutleaf groundcherry
local: Asisiu, kugut, potokan, sisiu, tutulakak, tino tino
stop: Pull it before the papery lanterns ripen, and keep it out of tomato, eggplant and pepper fields, where it carries the same insects and viruses.

name: Doveweed
stop: It roots from its creeping stems: pull whole plants and carry them out of the field instead of leaving them on the soil.

name: Eclipta zippeliana
stop: It sprouts on moist, open soil: flood the paddy early and pull it before it seeds.

name: Fringed spiderflower
local: Apoy apoyan, balabalanoyan, tantandok, sili silihan
stop: Pull it before the long pods split; it seeds within a few weeks and comes back in flushes after rain, so mulch the rows.

name: Giant salvinia
stop: Scoop it off the water, screen the inlet, and never move water plants from a pond that has it; a small piece starts a new mat.

name: Giant sensitive plant
local: Aroma, kapit kabag, kipi kipi, makahiya, makahiyang lalaki
stop: Slash it before it flowers and keep cutting the regrowth; a dense cover crop keeps the thorny tangles from coming back.

name: Hedyotis biflora
local: Dalumbang, kaddok na kalinga, palarapdap, pisak, pisek
stop: It grows on moist bunds and dry spots in the paddy: level the field, flood early and pull it before it seeds.

name: Diamond flower
local: Dalumbang, kaddok na kalinga,palarapdap, pisak, pisek
stop: It grows on moist bunds and dry spots in the paddy: level the field, flood early and pull it before it seeds.

name: Snake needle grass
stop: It grows on moist bunds and dry spots in the paddy: level the field, flood early and pull it before it seeds.

name: Desert horse purslane
stop: Hoe it while small, on a dry day, and carry it off; the fleshy stems root again if left on wet soil.

name: Ceylon hydrolea
stop: Pull it from wet edges and canals, and keep the paddy flooded early.

name: Indian heliotrope
local: Ar aritos, bahu baho, buntot leon, elepante, kambra kambra, higad higaran
stop: Pull or hoe it young and mulch the rows; do not let the curled flower spikes seed.

name: Indian jointvetch
stop: Pull it before its pods ripen; its seed mixes with harvested grain, so clean the seed you keep.

name: Water spinach
stop: Pull the runners out at land preparation and keep canals clean; stem pieces root again in wet soil.

name: Sparrow false pimpernel
stop: It thrives in saturated, not flooded, mud: keep water over the soil early and pull it young, before the tiny pods ripen.

name: Prostrate false pimpernel
stop: It thrives in saturated, not flooded, mud: keep water over the soil early and pull it young, before the tiny pods ripen.

name: Littlebell
local: Aurora, bangbangau, kamkamote, koskusipa, kupit kupit, halobagbug, muti muti
stop: Pull the vines before they climb the crop and before the seed capsules ripen.

name: Wingleaf primrose willow
stop: Flood the field early, pull it young, and spare the small black Altica beetle, which eats its leaves.

name: Mexican primrose willow
stop: Flood the field early, pull it young, and spare the small black Altica beetle, which eats its leaves.

name: Perennial water primrose
local: Kahoy kahoy, malapako, tina tina, sigang dagat
stop: Flood the field early, pull it young, and spare the small black Altica beetle, which eats its leaves.

name: Sensitive plant
local: Bain bain, hibi hibi, huya huya, kipi kipi, makahiya, makahiyang babae
stop: Dig it out with its taproot while young; slashing alone lets it grow back. Gloves help with the thorns.

name: Brazil jute
local: Anabo, bakembakes, bulbulin, buluhan, bulubuluhan, lapnis, pang balius, labog labog, tambaking
stop: Pull it young from bunds and field edges; older plants turn woody and hard to pull.

name: Malachra fasciata
stop: Pull it young from bunds and field edges; older plants turn woody and hard to pull.

name: Melochia concatenata
stop: Cut and dig it out of bunds and edges before it turns woody, and keep the field edges slashed.

name: Kidney leaf morning glory
stop: Pull the creeping stems out with their roots before they spread along bunds and moist edges.

name: Niruri
local: kurukalunggai, malakirum kirum, ngingihel, sampasampalukan, san pedro, sursampalok, talikod, taltalikod, turutalikod
stop: Hoe it young and mulch the rows; it ripens seed within weeks under its branches.

name: Common purslane
stop: Hoe it on a dry, sunny day and take it off the field; fleshy pieces left on moist soil root again.

name: Jute mallow
stop: Pull it young in upland fields, before the long pods ripen.

name: Sessile joyweed
stop: Pull it out with its creeping stems and keep bunds and wet edges clean; stem pieces root again.

name: Slender amaranth
local: Alom alom, ayang babae, halom, kilitis, kalunai, kudiapa, kulitis, uray babae
stop: Hoe or pull it before it flowers; one plant drops many thousands of tiny seeds.

name: Sphaeranthus africanus
stop: Pull it from moist edges and dry patches before it flowers; early flooding holds it back.

name: Spiny amaranth
local: Alayon, ayang lalaki, ayantoto, baoan, bayambang, harum, gitingiting, kalitis, kalunai, kuanton, kudiapa, kulitis, taikada, uray
stop: Hoe or pull it before it flowers, wearing gloves for the spines; one plant drops many thousands of tiny seeds.

name: Texasweed
stop: Flood early and pull it young, before its seed pods ripen and mix into the harvest.

name: Valley redstem
stop: Keep standing water early and pull it before the many small seed capsules along its stem ripen.

name: Dwarf water clover
stop: It spreads by creeping stems in shallow water: rake out the runners at land preparation and keep the water deep early.

name: Water lettuce
stop: Scoop it out of canals and ponds, screen the water inlet, and compost it away from the water; each plant sends out new ones on runners.

name: Wild bushbean
stop: Pull it before its pods ripen and keep field edges clean.

name: Yellow velvetleaf
stop: Dig out whole plants with their base before they flower, and screen the water inlet; its seed heads float into new fields.

name: Itchgrass
hint: A tall, stiff grass whose leaf sheaths carry glassy hairs that prick and itch the skin, topped by a thin, round, jointed spike.
stop: Never let it set seed: pull or slash it before it flowers, clean the harrow, planter and sheller after a weedy field, and plant a crop or cover crop that closes over the ground fast.

name: Cogon
local: Kogon, kugon, gogon, ilib, panaw, parang
hint: Upright grass with stiff leaves that have a pale midrib and rough edges, tough white runners underground, and fluffy silvery white flower spikes.
stop: Plow and harrow two or three times in the dry season to bring the runners up to dry, then shade it out with a crop, a legume cover crop or trees; it does not stand shade.

name: Wild sugarcane
hint: Very tall clumps like a thin wild sugarcane, with sharp edged leaves, fluffy white plumes and deep spreading runners.
stop: Cut the clumps low and dig out the base, then plant a crop or cover that shades the ground; burning only clears the top, and it comes back from the base.

name: Johnson grass
hint: Tall grass like a wild sorghum, with wide leaves that have a white midrib, a loose purplish seed head and thick white runners underground.
stop: Plow out the runners in dry weather and leave them to dry in the sun; never let it seed, and do not carry soil with its runners to another field.

name: Para grass
hint: Coarse creeping grass that roots at its hairy joints and forms thick mats in wet ground, with a seed head of short side branches.
stop: Rake out and dry the creeping stems, drain wet spots where you can, and keep canals and edges slashed.

name: Swollen fingergrass
hint: Tufted grass with flattened stems and a top of 6 to 15 purplish, feathery fingers spread like an open hand.
stop: Hoe it young and mow field edges and roadsides before the feathery heads ripen.

name: Whitehead spikesedge
hint: Low sedge with a three sided stem ending in one round, white flower head with three leafy bracts under it.
stop: It spreads by short runners: hoe it out with its base, mulch the rows, and keep paths mowed low.

name: Siam weed
hint: Rambling shrub up to 2 m with arrow shaped, three veined leaves in pairs that smell strong when crushed, and pale mauve to white flower tufts.
stop: Slash it before it flowers and dig out the crowns; a legume cover crop or quick shade keeps it from coming back.

name: Mile a minute vine
hint: Fast twining vine with heart shaped leaves in pairs and small clusters of white flowers that blanket shrubs and young trees; Mikania micrantha looks almost the same.
stop: Pull the vines off the crop and dig out the base; cut pieces root again, so do not leave them on moist ground.

name: Billygoat weed
hint: Soft, hairy herb with paired, egg shaped, toothed leaves, a goat like smell when crushed, and small fluffy blue to white flower heads.

sources.label: Stuartxchange, Philippine Medicinal Plants: Bulak manok

stop: Hoe or pull it before it flowers; it seeds in about 6 weeks, so mulch and an early weeding stop the next flush.

name: Spanish needle
local: Dadayem, puriket, pisau pisau, tubak tubak
hint: Upright herb with leaves split into 3 to 5 toothed parts, small white and yellow flower heads, and black needle seeds that stick to clothes.
stop: Pull it before the black, hooked seeds ripen; they stick to clothes and animals and travel to the next field.

name: Gallant soldier
hint: Soft, branching herb with paired, toothed, egg shaped leaves and tiny flower heads of 5 short white rays around a yellow center.
stop: Hoe or pull it while small and mulch the beds; it can seed within a month.

name: Tropical chickweed
hint: Low creeping herb with thin stems, small round leaves in pairs and tiny white flowers; its sticky seeds cling to clothes.
stop: Pull the mats before they flower and mulch the beds; it thrives in cool, moist upland fields.

name: Nodeweed
hint: Upright herb with paired, three veined, toothed leaves and small yellow flower heads tucked right at the leaf joints.
stop: Hoe it young and mulch the rows; do not let the seeds tucked at the leaf joints ripen.

name: Asthma weed
hint: Low, hairy herb with reddish stems that bleed white milky sap and round clusters of tiny greenish flowers at the leaf joints.

sources.label: Stuartxchange, Philippine Medicinal Plants: Gatas gatas

stop: Hoe or pull it young, before the tiny flower clusters seed, and mulch the beds.

name: Coat buttons
hint: Creeping, hairy herb with coarsely toothed paired leaves and a single flower head on a long stalk, with 5 short cream rays around a yellow center.

sources.label: Stuartxchange, Philippine Medicinal Plants: Coat buttons

stop: Dig it out with its roots, since it spreads by creeping stems, and mulch the rows.

name: Common wireweed
hint: Stiff, woody based shrublet with narrow toothed leaves and small yellow flowers at the leaf joints; the tough stems are hard to pull.
stop: Pull or dig it out while young, before the stems turn woody, and slash plantation rows before it seeds.

name: Caesar weed
hint: Woody shrub with rough, shallowly lobed leaves, small pink flowers, and burr fruits with hooked spines that stick to clothes.
stop: Dig it out young and slash it before the hooked burrs ripen; they cling to animals and clothes.

name: Lantana
hint: Prickly stemmed shrub with rough, strong smelling leaves and flat clusters of small yellow, orange and pink flowers that turn into black berries.
stop: Cut it low and dig out the crowns, then keep slashing the regrowth; birds spread its berries, so take out fruiting plants first.

name: Bush mint
hint: Strong smelling, hairy herb up to 2 m with square stems, toothed paired leaves and small blue purple flowers.

sources.label: Stuartxchange, Philippine Medicinal Plants: Suob kabayo

stop: Slash or pull it before it flowers and keep field edges clean; it seeds heavily on open, dry ground.

name: Creeping woodsorrel
hint: Low creeping herb with clover like leaves of three heart shaped leaflets, a sour taste and small yellow five petaled flowers.

sources.label: Stuartxchange, Philippine Medicinal Plants: Taingang daga

stop: Dig it out with its root, since it grows back from the base, and mulch the beds; its pods throw seed a long way.

name: Little ironweed
hint: Upright herb with alternate egg shaped leaves and many tiny purple, thistle like flower heads that turn into fluffy seeds.

sources.label: Stuartxchange, Philippine Medicinal Plants: Agas moro

stop: Hoe or pull it before its tiny purple heads turn to fluff.

name: Lilac tasselflower
local: Tagulinaw, cetim, kipot kipot, lamlampaka, libun
hint: Small herb with purplish backed leaves that clasp the stem and slender pink to purple tassel like flower heads.
stop: Pull it before the tassels turn to fluff, which the wind carries to new fields.

name: Blue snakeweed
hint: Woody based herb with toothed leaves and long, thin, whip like spikes that open a few small blue flowers at a time.
stop: Dig it out with its woody base and slash plantation paths before it seeds.

name: Elephant foot
hint: Flat rosette of rough, hairy, tongue shaped leaves pressed to the ground, with stiff forked stems carrying small purple flower heads.

sources.label: Stuartxchange, Philippine Medicinal Plants: Dila dila

stop: Dig out the flat rosettes with their roots; slashing misses them because they lie on the ground.

name: Stinking passion flower
local: Prutas baguio, marya marya, pasyonaryang mabaho, kurombot, lurunggut
hint: Climbing vine with coiled tendrils, three lobed hairy leaves that smell bad, white and purple fringed flowers, and small fruits wrapped in a lacy husk.

sources.label: Stuartxchange, Philippine Medicinal Plants: Prutas baguio

stop: Pull the vines off the crop and dig out the base; birds spread its fruit.

name: Black nightshade
hint: Soft upright herb with egg shaped leaves, small white star flowers with yellow centers and clusters of shiny black berries; the unripe berries are poisonous.

sources.label: Stuartxchange, Philippine Medicinal Plants: Lubi lubi

stop: Pull it before the berries ripen, and keep it out of tomato, eggplant and pepper fields, where it carries the same pests and diseases.

name: Spreading hogweed
hint: Spreading herb with thick reddish stems, paired round leaves pale underneath, tiny pink flowers on long thin stalks and sticky fruits.
stop: Dig it out with its thick root before it seeds; the sticky seeds cling to clothes and tools.

name: Sickle senna
hint: Bushy, bad smelling herb with leaves of 3 pairs of rounded leaflets, bright yellow flowers in pairs and long, thin, curved pods.

sources.label: Stuartxchange, Philippine Medicinal Plants: Katandang aso

stop: Pull or slash it before its long pods ripen; the hard seeds last years in the soil.

name: Silver cockscomb
hint: Upright herb with narrow leaves and pointed, silvery white to pink flower spikes shaped like candle flames.
stop: Pull it before the spikes seed, and keep it off the field edges.

name: Forked fern
hint: Ground fern that forms thick, springy tangles, with stiff fronds that fork again and again and a small bud in each fork.
stop: Slash and dig out the tangles, then lime and feed the soil and plant a cover crop; it takes over where the soil is poor and sour.

name: Chinese violet
hint: Low, sprawling herb with soft, egg shaped leaves in pairs and white or pale purple bell shaped flowers along one side of the stalk; it grows even in shade.
stop: Pull or slash it before it seeds and grow a cover crop; stem pieces root again, so carry them off.
